newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BORUSSIA DORTMUND PEN PICTURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BORUSSIA DORTMUND PEN PICTURES.

text.p: Pen pictures of Borussia Dortmund players ahead of Saturday's German first division match against Borussia Moenchengladbach:
Stefan Klos. Goalkeeper. Age 25. Not the largest of keepers at 1.82 metres but has turned into one of Dortmund's key players since he joined in 1988. An under-21 international.
Matthias Sammer. Libero. 29. One of Germany's most influential players during last year's European championship triumph. He is very good at going forward as well as defending.

Juergen Kohler. Defender. 31. Germany's most experienced defender had said he would quit the international game after bowing out of Euro 96 with injury but has changed his mind and may go on to the next World Cup finals. Key man-to-man marker. Played for Bayern Munich before joining Juventus and then Dortmund.
Paul Lambert. Midfielder. 27. Scottish international who joined on a free transfer from Motherwell at start of season. Has produced some impressive performances.
Joerg Heinrich. Wing-back. 26. German international who operates on the left-hand side. Came from Freiburg in 1995 and has played for national side.
Lars Ricken. Midfielder. 20. Burst into the first team while still at school and has had to combine his studies with professional football. He has ability to go forward and score goals.
Knut Reinhardt. Midfielder. 28. German international came to Dortmund from Bayer Leverkusen in 1991. Determined player who has scored once this season.

Stefan Reuter. Wing-back. 30. An important part of German national team at Euro 96. One of the fastest players in the game, he usually operates down the right but is flexible enough to take on the libero role on occasions. Missed European quarter-final in midweek because of suspension. One goal so far this term.

Andy Moeller. Midfielder. 29. German international and former Juventus player who suffered many ups-and-downs in his career. Major disappointment at 1994 World Cup but bounced back at Euro 96. Moeller is the key playmaker who can also score spectacular goals. Four so far this term.
Paulo Sousa. 26. Experienced Portugese international who has been suffering with calf injury lately. Came from Juventus in 1996.

Stephane Chapuisat. Forward. 27. Swiss international who has a reputation for scoring goals but also for being a tough customer despite his relatively small frame. Club's top goalscorer with eight goals this season.
Heiko Herrlich. Forward. 25. German international who came from Borussia Moenchengladbach in controversial circumstances in 1995. Seven goals this season.

Karlheinz Riedle. Striker. 31. Former Lazio player who used to be major figure in German national team but has been hampered by injuries in last few seasons. Returning to his best with six goals so far this season.
